note: Short topical-guide entries for the canonical theme ids used across all four volumes. Chapter references for each topic are computed from the chapters already tagged with it — not hand-curated here.

topics.name: Faith
topics.blurb: A hope for things not seen which are true — the first principle of the gospel, and the power by which prophets part seas, still storms, and move mountains.

topics.name: Obedience
topics.blurb: Keeping the commandments not from compulsion but from love — 'I will go and do' is the record's recurring pattern of willing submission to God.

topics.name: Covenant
topics.blurb: A two-way promise with God, sealed by ordinance — baptism, the sacrament, and the many covenants that bind a scattered people back to their Maker.

topics.name: Deliverance
topics.blurb: God rescuing His people from bondage, sea, sword, or sin — from the Red Sea to the escape from King Noah's guards.

topics.name: Atonement
topics.blurb: Christ's infinite sacrifice, which alone satisfies justice and opens the door to mercy — the doctrine every prophet in the record ultimately teaches.

topics.name: Repentance
topics.blurb: Godly sorrow that leads to change — the cry of every prophet from Enoch to Alma, and the door back into covenant after sin.

topics.name: Prophecy
topics.blurb: Words spoken by the Spirit of foretelling — of Christ's birth and death, of nations rising and falling, given long before the events themselves.

topics.name: Revelation
topics.blurb: God speaking to His children — by vision, by the still small voice, by the Urim and Thummim, or by the whisper of the Spirit to an open heart.

topics.name: Prayer
topics.blurb: The soul's communication with God — from Enos's day-long wrestle to the Lord's Prayer to Joseph Smith's first vocal prayer in a grove.

topics.name: Records & Scripture
topics.blurb: The keeping, preserving, and passing down of sacred writings — plates, scrolls, and books — so that later generations would not dwindle in unbelief.

topics.name: The Pride Cycle
topics.blurb: Prosperity breeds pride, pride brings destruction, destruction brings humility, humility brings prosperity again — the Book of Mormon's central warning, repeated for a thousand years.

topics.name: Humility
topics.blurb: A meek and teachable heart before God — the poor in spirit of the Zoramites, and the posture the proud must relearn again and again.

topics.name: Charity
topics.blurb: The pure love of Christ, which 'suffereth long, and is kind' — Mormon and Paul both call it the greatest of all gifts, without which all else is nothing.

topics.name: Missionary Work
topics.blurb: Carrying the gospel to others, often at great cost — the sons of Mosiah among the Lamanites, the apostles across the Roman world, and every era of the Restoration.

topics.name: Conversion
topics.blurb: A change of heart that turns a life toward God — Alma the Younger, Paul on the Damascus road, and thousands of Lamanites who buried their swords.

topics.name: Liberty
topics.blurb: Freedom to worship and govern according to conscience — the title of liberty, the reign of judges, and the price paid to defend both.

topics.name: War
topics.blurb: Armed conflict and its causes — pride, secret combinations, and dissension — set against the ideal of defensive war fought only to preserve family and freedom.

topics.name: Peace
topics.blurb: The rest that follows righteousness — the two centuries after Christ's visit when there was 'no contention in the land,' and the peace only the gospel can give.

topics.name: Justice & Mercy
topics.blurb: The law demands, mercy pleads — Alma teaches his son Corianton that only the Atonement lets mercy satisfy justice without robbing it.

topics.name: Resurrection
topics.blurb: The reuniting of body and spirit, made possible through Christ — 'as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive.'

topics.name: Judgment
topics.blurb: Standing before God to give an account — the great and last day toward which every prophet in scripture points.

topics.name: Apostasy
topics.blurb: A falling away from the fulness of the gospel — the pattern that follows every golden age in scripture, and the reason a Restoration was needed.

topics.name: Secret Combinations
topics.blurb: Oath-bound bands built on murder and gain, from Cain to the Gadianton robbers — Moroni's explicit warning to readers of our own day.

topics.name: Leadership
topics.blurb: Governing and serving others in righteousness — King Benjamin's labor with his own hands, Captain Moroni's zeal, and the judges who governed by the voice of the people.

topics.name: Family
topics.blurb: Parents, children, and covenant households — Lehi's family in the wilderness, the stripling warriors taught by their mothers, and the sealing power of the latter days.

topics.name: Gathering of Israel
topics.blurb: The scattered covenant people gathered again in the last days — the promise behind Zenos's olive tree and the stated purpose of the Book of Mormon itself.

topics.name: Enduring to the End
topics.blurb: Steadfastness in Christ through trial and time — 'press forward with a steadfastness in Christ,' Nephi's closing counsel to every reader.

topics.name: Hope
topics.blurb: A sure expectation of eternal life through Christ's Atonement — the anchor Moroni pairs with faith and charity as the whole of true religion.

topics.name: Baptism
topics.blurb: The covenant ordinance of water — a witness of a broken heart, a burial and rebirth, and the gate through which the doctrine of Christ begins.

topics.name: The Sacrament
topics.blurb: Bread and wine (or water) taken in remembrance of Christ's body and blood — instituted at Bountiful just as it was in Jerusalem, its prayers preserved word for word in Moroni.

topics.name: Priesthood
topics.blurb: The authority to act in God's name — conferred, ordered, and sometimes lost, from Melchizedek to Aaron to its restoration by angelic hands in 1829.

topics.name: Creation
topics.blurb: The ordering of the earth and the heavens by the word and power of God — the opening act of the Old Testament and the premise of every plan of salvation.

topics.name: The Fall
topics.blurb: Adam and Eve's transgression, which brought mortality and opposition into the world — 'Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy.'

topics.name: The Law of Moses
topics.blurb: The commandments, ordinances, and sacrifices given through Moses to point a covenant people to Christ until His coming fulfilled them.

topics.name: Kingship
topics.blurb: Rule by a single monarch — praised in righteous kings like David and Benjamin, warned against by Samuel and Mosiah alike as a burden easily abused.

topics.name: Exile & Captivity
topics.blurb: A covenant people carried from their land for unfaithfulness — Israel to Assyria, Judah to Babylon — and the promise of return that follows every exile.

topics.name: Wisdom
topics.blurb: Understanding that comes from God rather than the world — Solomon's plea at Gibeon, and the Proverbs' long argument that wisdom begins with fearing the Lord.

topics.name: Worship
topics.blurb: Reverence and devotion offered to God — in temple, tower, tent, and testimony, from burnt offerings to the sacrament table.

topics.name: The Messiah
topics.blurb: The promised Deliverer and Anointed One — prophesied by Isaiah and Zenos, born in Bethlehem, and identified throughout scripture as Jesus Christ.

topics.name: Miracles
topics.blurb: Mighty works wrought by faith and the power of God — healings, deliverances, and signs that testify of a God who has not stopped speaking.

topics.name: Parables
topics.blurb: Earthly stories carrying heavenly meaning — the Savior's chosen teaching method, from the sower to the prodigal son, and Zenos's allegory of the olive tree.

topics.name: Discipleship
topics.blurb: Following Christ in daily life — the twelve who left their nets, the Nephite disciples ordained at Bountiful, and every soul who takes His name upon them.

topics.name: Grace
topics.blurb: Enabling power and unmerited favor from Christ — Nephi's testimony that 'it is by grace that we are saved, after all we can do.'

topics.name: Divine Mission & Calling
topics.blurb: Being called and sent by God for a specific work — Moses to Pharaoh, the Twelve to all nations, Joseph Smith to translate and restore.

topics.name: The Second Coming
topics.blurb: Christ's promised return in glory to reign and to judge — anticipated by every prophet from Enoch to Moroni, and the great hope of the latter days.

topics.name: The Restoration
topics.blurb: The return of the fulness of the gospel, priesthood, and covenant in the latter days through the Prophet Joseph Smith, after centuries of apostasy.

topics.name: Zion
topics.blurb: The pure in heart gathered in unity — the city of Enoch taken up whole, the Nephites' two centuries of oneness, and the latter-day gathering to come.

topics.name: The Temple
topics.blurb: The house of the Lord — Solomon's temple, the temple at Bountiful where Christ appeared, and the Kirtland Temple where heaven opened again in 1836.

topics.name: Word of Wisdom
topics.blurb: The Lord's law of health revealed to Joseph Smith in 1833 — counsel on what to take into the body, and the promise of wisdom and strength to those who keep it.

topics.name: Consecration
topics.blurb: Devoting time, talents, and substance wholly to God's work — the Nephite economy of no rich and no poor, and the united order of the early Restoration.

topics.name: Agency
topics.blurb: The God-given power to choose — Lehi's teaching that men 'are free to choose liberty and eternal life... or to choose captivity and death.'

topics.name: Martyrdom
topics.blurb: Giving one's life for testimony of Christ — Abinadi in the fire, Stephen under stones, and Joseph and Hyrum Smith at Carthage.
